what_its_for: This gel is used to treat acne (pimples) on your face or body. It contains two medicines that work together: clindamycin is an antibiotic that kills the bacteria that cause acne, and benzoyl peroxide helps reduce oil, unclogs pores, and also fights bacteria.
how_to_take: Wash your hands before and after using this medicine. Gently wash and dry the skin you are treating before applying the gel. Apply a thin layer of the gel to the affected area(s) once or twice daily, as directed by your doctor. Do not get it in your eyes, mouth, nose, or lips. If you do, rinse with plenty of water right away. Avoid applying to broken, sunburned, or irritated skin.
dosing: Most people apply this gel once a day in the morning or as directed by their doctor. Some products may be used twice a day. Always follow your doctor's exact instructions. Use only enough to cover the affected area with a thin layer — using more will not make it work faster and may cause more irritation.
missed_dose: If you miss an application, apply it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed one and continue with your regular schedule. Do not apply a double amount to make up for a missed dose.
storage: Store this gel in the refrigerator (36°F to 46°F / 2°C to 8°C) or at room temperature as directed on your specific product label — storage requirements can vary by brand, so check your package instructions. Keep it away from heat and out of direct sunlight. Do not freeze. Keep out of reach of children. Throw away any unused gel after the expiration date on the package or within the time frame listed in your product instructions (often within 2 to 3 months of opening).
what_to_avoid: Avoid getting this gel in or near your eyes, mouth, nose, or any mucous membranes. Avoid using other harsh skin products, including strong soaps, astringents, toners, or other acne products (especially those containing alcohol or another benzoyl peroxide product), unless your doctor says it is okay — combining products can cause extra dryness and irritation. Be aware that this gel can bleach hair, fabrics, and colored clothing. Limit sun exposure and avoid tanning beds while using this medicine. Use a sunscreen and wear protective clothing when going outdoors because this medicine can make your skin more sensitive to the sun.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor if you notice: severe skin irritation, redness, burning, peeling, or swelling; signs of an allergic reaction such as hives, rash, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing; severe stomach pain, cramping, or bloody diarrhea (this could be a sign of a serious bowel problem called colitis, which can happen with clindamycin); or if your acne seems to be getting worse after several weeks of treatment.
when_it_works: Most people begin to notice some improvement in their acne within 4 to 6 weeks. However, it may take up to 8 to 12 weeks (about 2 to 3 months) of regular use to see the full benefit. Keep using it as directed even if you do not see immediate results. Do not stop using it without talking to your doctor first.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Talk to your doctor before using this medicine if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, as the safety of this combination product during pregnancy and breastfeeding is not fully established. Children: This medicine is generally not recommended for children under 12 years of age. Elderly patients: No special dose adjustments are typically needed, but elderly patients with sensitive skin should use with caution. People with inflammatory bowel disease or a history of colitis: Tell your doctor before using this medicine, as the clindamycin component may increase the risk of bowel problems.
